questions.question: In Python, a for loop iterates over each element in a sequence like a list or a string.
A while loop is the best choice when the number of iterations is known ahead of time.
The break statement immediately exits the loop, regardless of remaining iterations.
The continue statement ends all further execution of the loop and exits it entirely.
An else clause after a for loop in Python executes only when the loop has finished normally without encountering a break statement.
It is impossible to use nested loops in Python to iterate over more than two levels of data.
Using range(1, 10, 2) in a Python for loop generates the sequence of odd numbers from 1 to 9.
A for loop in Python can only iterate over lists and tuples, not other iterable types.
An infinite loop can be created using a while loop with a condition that always evaluates to True, such as 'while True:'.
Modifying a list by adding or removing elements during iteration in a for loop is a safe and recommended practice.
